expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response correctly rejects the customer's claim as proof. It explains: (1) the input entry only has appliedGuardrailDetails and invocationMetrics, no sensitiveInformationPolicy section, so no detection/masking is recorded; (2) sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits is 0 on input vs 1 on output; (3) the 85/228 guardrailCoverage matches the 85-char user message being guarded, consistent with expected text; (4) it infers (using 'almost certainly', 'I believe') that the model saw unmasked values since masked text would show tags like {CREDIT_DEBIT_CARD_NUMBER} rather than the actual values - framed as inference, not fact; (5) it ties the ambiguity to the GetGuardrail entities showing only 'type' and 'action' (action-only reading), explicitly calling this an observation with appropriate hedging ('I can't say why', 'two candidates'), not claiming AWS-documented behavior; (6) it does not call it 'detect mode'; (7) it recommends checking inputEnabled/outputEnabled and inputAction/outputAction explicitly; (8) it suggests the customer run ApplyGuardrail with source INPUT and compare, as a check for the customer to do themselves, not something the agent executes; (9) no raw account ID is printed (no specific card number was given in the prompt to leak, and none appears in response). The only expected item not explicitly addressed is citing 'LLM-GRD-003' control ID, which doesn't appear in the response at all - this is a miss, but it's a specific internal reference ID that may not be a universally expected format; given the rest of the substantive technical content aligns very well, this appears to be a partial gap. However, given the instruction to focus on substance, the response covers the core reasoning and caveats correctly, with the LLM-GRD-003 citation being the one clear miss.</reasoning>
